summary: Morris County tower built 1924 near Budd Lake, the state's only lookout with an Osborne fire finder; still active, seasonally staffed, top cab locked.

facts.design: 60-ft steel Aermotor tower with 7'x7' metal cab; carries an Osborne fire finder

access.note: Top cabin locked and a No Trespassing sign posted at the base, per a 2025 hiking guide. The guide says the sign is not enforced and that visitors can climb most of the way up. Active state fire tower.

visit.trail_note: Park at the end of the road and walk a short fire road to the base, per the 2023 NHLR visit report. The 2025 guide says visitors can climb most of the way up; the top cabin is locked.

events.note: Site known as the 95 Mile Tree Lookout, for its place on the old state turnpike; the register does not say a tower stood there then

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1924 notice and a 1925 clipping place the tower on Turkey Hill near Waterloo, on Waterloo Mountain. The register places it on the west shore of Budd Lake. Not reconciled: the sources do not say whether the tower moved or whether the clippings describe another structure. The story reports the disagreement.

The 2023 visit report says park at the end of Fire Tower Road; the 2025 guide says parking is at the end of Station Road. Both describe a short walk from a parking area, so the story uses general wording.

notes_for_editor: Staffing as_of is the April 2023 visit report; no newer staffing data found. Access level 'restricted' is inferred from active status and the locked cab. The 2025 guide says the No Trespassing sign is not enforced and that climbing most of the way up is possible, so the story reports that rather than calling the tower off-limits. The 1925 clipping's lookout details (season opening, visitor counts) are not used as Budd Lake events because the location conflicts. Brief height 18.0 m matches the register's 60 ft.
